raw_case_text:
A 47-year-old man living in the countryside with a history of exposure to cattle was admitted to our hospital with a 2-week history of abdominal distension and a 9-day history of fever. Initially, the patient also presented with fatigue, myalgia, and joint pain. Within 2 weeks, he lost 7.5 kg of body weight. His temperature reached 38.9 C for 9 days. Before he came to our hospital, he was treated in a local hospital for 9 days. His local test results showed that his blood culture was negative, and abdominal computed tomography (CT) showed splenic infarction and portal vein enlargement. The Brucella serum tube agglutination test (SAT) was negative (1:25). His symptoms had no improvement with 6-day ceftriaxone [2.0, quaque die, intra-veineuse drip (QD, iv. D)] treatment. Then, he was discharged from the local hospital and visited our hospital.
At admission, his physical examination results were as follows: blood pressure, 132/72 mmHg; high-grade fever, 39.0 C; tachycardia, 102 beats/min; submandibular, cervical, and axillary enlarged lymph nodes were 10-20 mm, soft, freely moveable, and nontender; he had hepatomegaly, with the liver felt 2.0 cm below the ribs; and splenomegaly, with the spleen felt 5.0 cm below the ribs.
The laboratory results were as follows: white blood cell counts of 3.2 x 109/L (normal range: 3.5-9.5) and hemoglobin of 100 (normal range: 130-175) g/L. Liver enzymes and cardiac enzymes were increased: aspartate aminotransferase of 329.9 (normal range: 15-40) U/L, alanine aminotransferase of 217.1 (normal range: 9-50) U/L, alkaline phosphatase of 417.4 (normal range: 45-125) U/L, and lactate dehydrogenase of 284 (normal range: 120-250) U/L. Pancreatic enzymes were increased: amylase of 151.8 (normal range: 35-135) U/L and lipase of 127.8 (normal range: 0-79) U/L. The tumor marker carbohydrate antigen (CA) 19-9 level was obviously increased at 240.1 (normal range: 0-37) U/mL. Brucella serum tests were sent again, and the results were as follows: STA was weakly positive (1:100), and Brucellosis antibody IgG was positive. Inflammatory marker levels were increased: C-reactive protein of 17.0 (normal range: 0-10) mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 72 (normal range: 0-15) mm/h, and ferritin of 897.3 (normal range: 20-300) mug/L. Abdominal ultrasound showed hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and multiple low-density lesions in the spleen. Enhanced abdominal CT showed hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, multiple low-density lesions in the spleen (prone to splenic infarction), portal vein enlargement, and a small amount of effusion in the pelvis ( Figure 1 ). Brucella abortus was cultured and isolated from blood after 5 days.
Because of the concerns about his long-term exposure to cattle, treatment after admission was started and consisted of doxycycline [0.1, bis in die, per os (BID, p.o.)] and streptomycin [15 mg/kg, quaque die, intramuscular injection (QD, IM)]. After verifying Brucella abortus infection by blood culture, rifampicin (0.6, QD, p.o.) was added to the combination therapy ( Figure 2 ). The body temperature of the patient recovered to the normal level after anti-brucellosis treatment for 6 days. After 8 days of treatment, blood tests and abdominal ultrasound were performed. The blood test results were as follows: CA 19-9 decreased to 70.1 U/L. Abdominal ultrasound showed hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and no low-density lesions in the spleen. The subsequent treatment with streptomycin was administered for 2 weeks, and the other two medicines were taken for 6 weeks. After 1 month of treatment, pancreatic enzymes levels and liver enzymes recovered to normal levels: the amylase 66 U/L, the lipase 55.2 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase 20 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 18 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase 88 U/L. After 6 weeks of treatment, CA 19-9 recovered to normal levels. Abdominal CT showed that the low-density lesions in the spleen were much less than the former ( Figure 3 ).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old man presented with a 2-week history of abdominal distension and a 9-day history of high fever.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 47-year-old man from the countryside developed abdominal distension 2 weeks prior to admission along with fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, and a 7.5 kg weight loss, followed by a 9-day history of fever peaking at 38.9 C. He had been hospitalized at a local hospital for 9 days where blood cultures and a Brucella serum tube agglutination test (1:25) were negative, abdominal CT showed splenic infarction and portal vein enlargement, and 6 days of IV ceftriaxone (2.0 g QD) failed to improve his symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resided in the countryside with a history of cattle exposure; prior 9-day local hospitalization treated with IV ceftriaxone.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for abdominal distension, high fever (up to 38.9 C), fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, and 7.5 kg weight loss over 2 weeks.

objective.physical_examination: Blood pressure 132/72 mmHg, temperature 39.0 C, heart rate 102 beats/min. Submandibular, cervical, and axillary lymphadenopathy (10-20 mm, soft, mobile, nontender). Hepatomegaly palpable 2.0 cm below the costal margin and splenomegaly palpable 5.0 cm below the costal margin.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 3.2 x 10^9/L (normal: 3.5-9.5), hemoglobin 100 g/L (normal: 130-175). Elevated liver, cardiac, and pancreatic enzymes: AST 329.9 U/L (normal: 15-40), ALT 217.1 U/L (normal: 9-50), ALP 417.4 U/L (normal: 45-125), LDH 284 U/L (normal: 120-250), amylase 151.8 U/L (normal: 35-135), lipase 127.8 U/L (normal: 0-79). Tumor marker CA 19-9 markedly elevated at 240.1 U/mL (normal: 0-37). Inflammatory markers elevated: CRP 17.0 mg/L (normal: 0-10), ESR 72 mm/h (normal: 0-15), ferritin 897.3 ug/L (normal: 20-300). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrated hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and multiple hypoechoic/low-density splenic lesions.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated hepatomegaly, splenomegaly with multiple low-density splenic infarction lesions, portal vein enlargement, and a small pelvic effusion.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Repeat Brucella standard tube agglutination (STA) test was weakly positive (1:100), Brucella IgG antibody was positive, and blood culture isolated Brucella abortus after 5 days of incubation, confirming acute brucellosis complicated by splenic infarction, hepatitis, mild pancreatitis, and elevated CA 19-9. Empiric oral doxycycline (0.1 g BID) and intramuscular streptomycin (15 mg/kg QD) were initiated at admission, with oral rifampicin (0.6 g QD) added after blood culture confirmation (streptomycin given for 2 weeks; doxycycline and rifampicin for 6 weeks). Fever resolved after 6 days; by day 8, CA 19-9 dropped to 70.1 U/L; at 1 month, liver and pancreatic enzymes normalized (amylase 66 U/L, lipase 55.2 U/L, AST 20 U/L, ALT 18 U/L, ALP 88 U/L); and after 6 weeks, CA 19-9 normalized and follow-up CT showed marked resolution of splenic infarction lesions.
